investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T21:32–21:39Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported Insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity. With 0 of 6 nodes able to schedule the pod and preemption offering no relief, the agent VM was never provisioned. As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never completed, and none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) to fail with all four fields missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required label or taint, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.
Tertiary — VM resource quota set too low for the current workload level: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may not have been scaled to match demand.
Quaternary — leaked or stuck remote agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1883), holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > used on the 2 eligible nodes), the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the scheduler message would need re-examination.
If the pod's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that it should match more than 2 nodes, the diagnosis shifts from capacity exhaustion to a configuration drift problem.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after clearing suspected zombie VMs succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, that would confirm leaked VMs as the primary cause rather than a hard capacity ceiling.

If the eval runner is found to have a bug that submits pods with incorrect resource requests (e.g., requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than intended), the root cause would be in the eval runner rather than cluster capacity.

If the three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) were submitted sequentially and each consumed a VM slot without releasing it, the failure pattern could be an eval-run ordering artifact rather than a pre-existing capacity shortage.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a timeout.
Add an eval that counts the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector and alerts if the eligible pool drops below a configured minimum (e.g., fewer than 2 nodes).
Add a zombie-VM detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and flags any that have been running beyond the expected eval cleanup window.

Add a latency-band eval for remote agent pod scheduling that warns if scheduling takes longer than a threshold (e.g., 30s) before the full outageLatencyMs is reached, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T21:34–21:39Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were populated, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node affinity/selector mismatch). No preemption victims were available. As a result, every eval attempt to provision a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~141–145 s), preventing the runner from reaching the state-polling phase and leaving all required evidence fields absent. This is a production infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval code defect.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the eligible scheduling pool to only 2 nodes. If this selector was recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective capacity could have dropped suddenly.

If each eval provisions its own pod and the cluster has limited kata VM slots, concurrent eval runs could exhaust capacity even if individual runs would succeed in isolation.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T21:32–21:39Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported Insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity. With 0 of 6 nodes able to schedule the pod and preemption offering no relief, the agent VM was never provisioned. As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never completed, and none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) to fail with all four fields missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required label or taint, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.
Tertiary — VM resource quota set too low for the current workload level: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may not have been scaled to match demand.
Quaternary — leaked or stuck remote agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1883), holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

If the pod's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that it should match more than 2 nodes, the diagnosis shifts from capacity exhaustion to a configuration drift problem.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-03 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. With no schedulable capacity and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately stuck as Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the agent pod never starts, so the eval runner never reaches the runtime test phase and produces no evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure signal; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes that satisfy the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity and no preemption victims.

SECONDARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded by the pod's affinity rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or were recently tightened, this could reduce effective capacity below the demand level.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user workloads may have left peer-pod VMs running without releasing their resource reservations, exhausting the pool without a corresponding increase in real load.

QUATERNARY — cluster node count insufficient for the current remote-agent workload: the 6-node cluster with only 2 affinity-eligible nodes may simply be undersized for concurrent eval probes plus any live user workloads sharing the same resource pool.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted on the affinity-eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota policy, admission webhook, or runtime class misconfiguration).
If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on an immediate re-run with the same cluster state, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a re-run, the root cause is specific to the runtime check rather than a shared pod scheduling constraint.
If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity are shown to actually be eligible (i.e., the affinity rules were recently relaxed), then node affinity misconfiguration is not a contributing factor.
If no zombie or leaked peer-pod VMs are found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the exhaustion is due to legitimate concurrent workload demand rather than resource leakage.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes and warns when available slots fall below a configured threshold, providing earlier warning before scheduling failures occur.
Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that fails fast (e.g., within 30s) if a remote-agent pod is not scheduled, rather than waiting for the full ~148s timeout, to reduce detection latency.
Add a zombie/leaked-pod detection eval that counts remote-agent pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable TTL and alerts when leaked pods are consuming VM slots.

Consider a synthetic canary eval that provisions and immediately tears down a single remote-agent pod on a scheduled interval to continuously validate scheduling headroom without accumulating resource debt.
